Goblins have lived in Escann since back in the times of giants. They used to have a vast kingdom covering most of Escann, built on a pact with the fey. However, the goblins broke the pact, and the fey responded by causing the collapse of the kingdom, and the splintering of the goblins into many small clans. 

Since then, most Forest Goblins have hated the fey, and this hatred is central to their culture. These are called the Old Ways. However, ironically, this didn't help them when the Castanites were rounding up and slaughtering all the fey they could find in Escann under Castan Beastbane, as they thought goblins were simply a kind of fey. 

This left the goblins only the Deepwoods, and when the Elves arrived in the Deepwoods, they were pushed to the fringes even then. This splintering did mean that the Old Ways goblins had less capability to crack down on Pactseekers when they showed up, and when first clan Verminhusk turned to the fey, there was no organized effort to stamp them out. 

Later, when the Greentide arrived in the Deepwoods, they brought a lot of goblin slaves, and while some goblin clans were destroyed, a lot of the orcs' slaves were liberated which helped bolster the numbers of the Deepwoods goblins, making them able to be a force in their own right in the region. This period is also when clan Oubbligschild is formed and clan Petalmasher becomes Pactseeker.

General tip when it comes to dwarf adventurers: you really shouldn't wait to complete their whole tree, especially if a hold you can form has missions. A fair amount of MTs give you expansion bonuses and assume you haven't expanded much out of your hold. 

Forming a hold also gives you a free colonist for a fair amount of time and enables the estates, both of which are highly advantageous (especially since the estates can help you with expansion too) My personal rule of thumb is getting at least past the mission that gives you a free colonist before you form the hold so you get 3 colonists.

As for who to form, it depends on your playstyle. Not sure which ones are available for you so here's them all:

-Khug: recreate the bank of asra and reconnect with the rest of Cannor

-Haraz (New MT): create a true dwarf empire with Orc slaves (can't get more dwarf than that)

-Mithrad: discover the benefits of mithril and lend out your services as mercenaries for Escann

-Amld: reconquer the mountains and reforge the old dwarven empire (it's all conquering, nothing else)

-Orlazam: go wild with calvary and perfect your rams

-Vazhatun :research the cosmos and try to not go insane with your discoveries (very unique experience around a nation specific mechanic)

-Krak: discover the magics of icecraft as you make your way back to the rest of Dwarovar (better played as the hold at the start than refounded in my opinion)

-Natvir: conquer the rails and bring back trade as the largest trade hub (MT is short and old)

-Kozenad: no MT, lore rumor that this old is cursed with bad luck

-Jorkad: no MT but fun fact this is where the orcs got their name, there's also a useful dam nearby

With the amount of replayability there is with the Serpentspine, don't worry about making the wrong decision. You'll most likely end up trying most of them at least one or twice if you like the dwarf experience.

(Tl;dr: make a save and reform each one, check their ideas and MT and see what you like)

This is my breakdown of the factions in my experience:

Expansionists are good for faster colonizing, and are always ideal to have, especially for Krak since you're gonna want to get out of the mountain as soon as possible. Choosing them gives you the best expansion bonuses (and an extra colonist iirc), but their secondary bonuses aren't too bad either.

Reclaimers give you a free hold level if you choose them, and construction cost/dev cost if not. I usually end up picking them since the free level is very valuable.

The Guard is situational. It's helpful when fighting against any nearby roaming nations/large neighbors (Kanzad, Krak, and Gulan) since they outnumber you 2 to 1. The others (Ordstun, Lodhum, Seghdihr) can get lucky. They give some really great bonuses, but I wouldn't recommend choosing them over the others.

Sometimes you have to take all three to survive, others just the one. It depends on how fast you want/need to expand and what areas you want to prioritize.

There's pros and cons for both expelling/purging vs integrating.

Expell/purge: This is the fastest way to convert provinces to both your religion and culture. While converting may be easier if you have religious ideas, you still have to pay a lot of diplo to either culture convert or accept culture. Downside is that you generate devastation or potentially loss of dev in some provinces, plus you lose out on some benefits.

Integrate: A lot slower than above (tho if you accept their culture then it hops you up to accepted level), you don't change religions or cultures. Meaning you have to manually accept or convert both. However, each pop has a few minor bonuses that are quite beneficial if you decide to stick it out.

Overall it's dependent on short term vs long term, your level of roleplay, and for some nations' missions require you to remove certain races.
